record.paper_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
record.original_question: In the unramified local setting where E_v/F_v is an unramified quadratic extension of residue characteristic not 2, ψ_v and μ_v are unramified, V_v admits a self-dual lattice with hyperspecial stabilizer, and Π_v together with the chosen vectors are spherical of norm 1, prove the explicit formula Conjecture 2.4 for the local period integral I_v, namely that I_v equals (L(1, M∨_{GL(V_v)}) / L(1, M∨_{U(V_v)})) · (L(1/2, Π_v × σΠ∨_v × μ_v^{-1}) / L(1, Π_v, Ad)).

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.4. Suppose that ... Then Iv(fv, f′v, φv, φ′v) = L(1, M∨GL(Vv))/L(1, M∨U(Vv)) · L(1/2, Πv × σΠ∨v × µ−1v)/L(1, Πv, Ad).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let F be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic different from 2, and let E/F be an unramified quadratic field extension, with non-trivial Galois automorphism σ. Let ψ : F → C^× be an unramified non-trivial additive character, and let μ : E^× → C^× be an unramified character whose restriction to F^× equals the quadratic character associated with E/F.

Let V be a finite-dimensional Hermitian space over E that contains a self-dual O_E-lattice L; let U(V) denote the corresponding unitary group, whose stabilizer K_V of L is a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup. Let GL(V) denote the general linear group of V regarded as an E-vector space. For an irreducible admissible representation Π of GL(V)(E), assume Π is unramified (spherical with respect to a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup), and choose a K-fixed vector of norm 1 with respect to a fixed invariant inner product. Let σΠ^∨ denote the representation g ↦ Π^∨(σ(g)).

Let M_{GL(V)}^∨ and M_{U(V)}^∨ denote the dual motives attached to GL(V) and U(V), with associated local L-factors L(s, M^∨_{GL(V)}) and L(s, M^∨_{U(V)}). Let L(s, Π × σΠ^∨ × μ^{-1}) be the twisted Rankin–Selberg L-factor (the local Asai-type L-factor entering the twisted GGP problem), and let L(s, Π, Ad) be the local adjoint L-factor of Π.

Local period integral. Using ψ and μ, define the unramified local period integral I(f, f′, φ, φ′) attached to the twisted GGP problem on the pair (GL(V), U(V)) with input vectors f, f′ in Π, Π^∨ and Schwartz–Bruhat data φ, φ′ associated to the Weil representation, normalized so that the K-fixed unramified test data have norm 1.

Problem. Prove that, with the above unramified normalizations and spherical input data of norm 1,
 I(f, f′, φ, φ′) = [ L(1, M^∨_{GL(V)}) / L(1, M^∨_{U(V)}) ] · [ L(1/2, Π × σΠ^∨ × μ^{-1}) / L(1, Π, Ad) ].
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on the twisted Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture in the unramified case (e.g., the 2023 preprint "Twisted Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for unramified quadratic extensions" and a 2025 follow-up on Asai L-values) establishes global results under assumptions that include this explicit unramified local integral identity as a hypothesis; the local identity itself is stated as a conjecture and is not proved in general. Thus the explicit unramified local formula appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Twisted Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for unramified quadratic extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 1.5 (refined version) relates the period integral explicitly to L-functions ... assuming Conjecture 1.4 holds. Conjecture 1.4 (the local integral formula) remains open as a general statement.
status_evidence.claim: The unramified explicit local formula is used as a hypothesis and is not proved in general.

status_evidence.title: Central values of Asai L-functions and twisted Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the global twisted GGP conjecture... rather than deriving explicit local integral-to-L-function ratio formulas for unramified settings.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work proves global statements but does not prove the explicit unramified local formula.
